title: Roots Blower
model_title: Roots (Rotary Lobe) Blower — Tri-Lobe, Timing Gears

introduction.definition: A Roots blower uses two lobed rotors turning in opposite directions, kept in step by timing gears and never touching. Each rotor carries pockets of air from the inlet to the outlet around the casing. There is no internal compression: pressure rises when the pocket opens to the discharge and higher-pressure gas flows back into it.
key_points: Never throttle the outlet — use a relief valve
introduction.summary: A Roots blower moves air with two lobed rotors that turn in opposite directions without touching, kept in step by timing gears. Air is trapped between each rotor and the casing and carried from the inlet to the outlet; there is no internal compression — the pressure rises when the pocket opens to the higher-pressure discharge (backflow). Used for low pressure ratios such as aeration and pneumatic conveying.

video_tutorials.title: Roots Blower — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Roots Blower.
A Roots blower uses two lobed rotors turning in opposite directions, kept in step by timing gears and never touching.
Each rotor carries pockets of air from the inlet to the outlet around the casing.
There is no internal compression: pressure rises when the pocket opens to the discharge and higher-pressure gas flows back into it.
Typical applications include aeration of wastewater (biological treatment); pneumatic conveying of powders; fluidising air, combustion air; vacuum duty (mechanical boosters).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Blower Casing (Rotor Housing), Drive-Side End Plate (hidden in cutaway), Drive Rotor (tri-lobe) & Shaft, Driven Rotor (tri-lobe) & Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Roots Blower works.
Air enters the inlet at the top.
Each rotor traps a pocket of air against the casing wall.
The pockets are carried round to the outlet; the rotors mesh in the middle without touching.
Timing gears keep the rotors in exact phase.
Silencers reduce the pulsation noise.

video_tutorials.title: Roots Blower — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Roots Blower.
Check gearbox oil level and belt tension.
Change gear oil; clean inlet filter.
Replace bearings and seals; check rotor clearances.
Watch for rotor contact: knocking, seizure. Common cause: bearing failure, overheating (over-pressure), gear wear.
Watch for overheating: high discharge temperature. Common cause: excess pressure, blocked filter.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why do Roots blower rotors never touch?
options: Timing gears keep them in phase with small clearances

questions.question: Is there internal compression in a Roots blower?
options: No — pressure rises when the pocket opens to discharge

questions.question: What must be installed on the discharge?
options: A throttle valve to control flow
questions.explanation: Positive displacement — closing the outlet causes overpressure.
